title: [Kernel][FP8] Initial support with dynamic per-tensor scaling (#4118)
reported_gain: N/A (enabling PR; author's own numbers show FP8 SLOWER than BF16: 1.47s->1.66s E2E, TTFT 28.8->38.8ms. No speedup achieved yet; this PR adds the FP8 path to unblock follow-up optimizations.)
note: Initial FP8 (dynamic per-tensor scaling) enablement: loads FP16/BF16 checkpoints, quantizes weights to FP8 post-load, computes activation scales each forward pass. Enabled via --quantization fp8. The author's own measurements show FP8 is currently SLOWER than BF16 (Mistral-7B 1xH100: BF16 1.47s vs FP8 1.66s; comaniac's run: FP16 TTFT 28.8ms / ITL 8.5ms vs FP8 38.8ms / 10.2ms) because activation quantization adds large overhead. The author explicitly states 'we haven't achieved a decent performance with this FP8 support' and merges it to unblock follow-up optimizations. There is therefore no speedup gain to record; the eventual 2x-class FP8 wins land in later kernel PRs, not here. No timing experiment.
environment: reported-only: author's published GPU numbers; measured arms pending on GPU box
